meaningEn: (manner) twinkling, sparkling; of small lights, stars, polished things; pairs with 빛나다 or 반짝이다.
exampleKo: 어두운 밤하늘에 별들이 반짝반짝 빛나서 정말 아름다웠어.
exampleEn: The stars twinkled beautifully in the dark night sky, making it truly gorgeous.

meaningEn: (manner) flashing, gleaming brightly; lightning, gold, a shined car; pairs with 번쩍이다. Bigger/harsher than 반짝반짝.
exampleKo: 새 차가 햇빛에 번쩍번쩍 빛나서 눈이 부셨어.
exampleEn: The new car gleamed brightly in the sunlight, dazzling my eyes.

meaningEn: (manner) blinking, flickering; a turn signal, a dying bulb, eyes; pairs with 깜빡거리다. NOTE: 깜빡하다 also means to forget momentarily.
exampleKo: 오래된 전구가 깜빡깜빡하더니 결국 꺼져버렸어.
exampleEn: The old light bulb flickered a few times and then finally went out.

meaningEn: (manner) multicolored, patterned in many bright colors; pairs with 알록달록하다.
exampleKo: 아이들 옷이 알록달록해서 정말 예쁘고 귀여워 보여.
exampleEn: The children's clothes are so colorful, they look really pretty and adorable.

meaningEn: (manner) splashed with reds and yellows; classic word for autumn foliage; pairs with 울긋불긋하다.
exampleKo: 가을 산은 단풍으로 울긋불긋 아름다운 옷을 입었네.
exampleEn: The autumn mountain dressed itself in beautiful, colorful fall foliage.

meaningEn: (manner) shimmering faintly, hazily flickering in sight or in memory; pairs with 아른거리다. (e.g. a face 아른거리다 = can't stop picturing it.)
exampleKo: 고향에 계신 할머니 얼굴이 자꾸 아른아른 떠올라.
exampleEn: My grandmother's face back home keeps shimmering faintly in my mind.

meaningEn: (manner) heart pounding with excitement or nerves; pairs with 두근거리다. The single most-used emotion mimetic.
exampleKo: 첫 데이트라니, 아침부터 가슴이 두근두근 떨렸어.
exampleEn: It's our first date, so my heart has been pounding with excitement since this morning.

meaningEn: (manner) heart thumping lightly and fast; cuter, smaller-scale than 두근두근; pairs with 콩닥거리다.
exampleKo: 아기가 엄마 품에서 콩닥콩닥 심장이 뛰고 있었어.
exampleEn: The baby's heart was thumping lightly and fast in its mother's arms.

meaningEn: (manner) on edge, nervously watching something risky unfold; pairs with 조마조마하다.
exampleKo: 시험 결과를 기다리는 동안 너무 조마조마했어.
exampleEn: I was so on edge while waiting for my test results.

meaningEn: (manner) emotion surging up all at once; tears rising, or a flash of anger; pairs with 울컥하다.
exampleKo: 친구의 진심 어린 말에 갑자기 눈물이 울컥 쏟아졌어.
exampleEn: At my friend's heartfelt words, tears suddenly welled up.

meaningEn: (manner) heart swelling with warmth, deeply moved; often 가슴이 뭉클하다; pairs with 뭉클하다.
exampleKo: 졸업식에서 부모님께 감사 인사를 전하니 가슴이 뭉클했어.
exampleEn: My heart swelled with warmth when I thanked my parents at graduation.

meaningEn: (manner) an electric, thrilling tingle; also a limb tingling; pairs with 짜릿하다.
exampleKo: 높은 곳에서 번지점프를 하니 온몸이 짜릿짜릿했어.
exampleEn: My whole body tingled with thrill after bungee jumping from a high place.

meaningEn: (manner) chills running over you from fear or cold; pairs with 오싹하다. A horror-movie word.
exampleKo: 한밤중에 으스스한 소리를 들으니 등골이 오싹오싹했어.
exampleEn: Hearing a creepy sound in the middle of the night sent chills down my spine.

meaningEn: (manner) a sudden eerie chill, blood running cold at something sinister; pairs with 섬뜩하다.
exampleKo: 어두운 골목에서 이상한 그림자를 보고 등골이 섬뜩했어.
exampleEn: I saw a strange shadow in the dark alley and felt a chill down my spine.

meaningEn: (manner) itchy; figuratively itching to do something you're holding back; pairs with 근질거리다. (e.g., 입이 근질근질 = dying to spill a secret).
exampleKo: 새로운 비밀을 알아서 입이 근질근질해서 참기 힘들어.
exampleEn: I know a new secret, and my mouth is itching to tell it, it's hard to hold back.

meaningEn: (manner) with a start; almost always 깜짝 놀라다 = to be startled. Also 깜짝 파티 = surprise party.
exampleKo: 뒤에서 갑자기 누가 내 이름을 불러서 깜짝 놀랐잖아.
exampleEn: Someone suddenly called my name from behind, and I was startled.

meaningEn: (manner) with a violent start, jumping in shock; stronger than 깜짝; often 화들짝 놀라다.
exampleKo: 인기척 없는 곳에서 고양이가 튀어나와서 화들짝 놀랐어.
exampleEn: A cat suddenly jumped out in a deserted place, and I jumped in shock.

meaningEn: (manner) flinching, a small startled recoil of the shoulders; pairs with 흠칫하다.
exampleKo: 갑자기 들리는 소리에 그는 흠칫 놀라 어깨를 움츠렸어.
exampleEn: He flinched at the sudden sound, recoiling his shoulders.

meaningEn: (manner) looking around restlessly, head turning to search; pairs with 두리번거리다.
exampleKo: 처음 온 도시에서 길을 잃어서 두리번두리번 주위를 살폈어.
exampleEn: I got lost in a new city and looked around restlessly.

meaningEn: (manner) fidgety with worry, unable to settle. WARNING: only used as 안절부절못하다; 안절부절하다 is incorrect Korean.
exampleKo: 중요한 발표를 앞두고 너무 긴장돼서 안절부절못하고 있었어.
exampleEn: I was fidgety with worry, unable to settle, because I was so nervous before an important presentation.

meaningEn: (sound) loud, uninhibited cackling laughter; pairs with 깔깔거리다.
exampleKo: 친구들과 재미있는 농담을 주고받으며 깔깔 웃었어.
exampleEn: I exchanged funny jokes with my friends and cackled with laughter.

meaningEn: (sound) giggling, a stifled laugh you're trying to hold in; pairs with 킥킥거리다.
exampleKo: 선생님 몰래 친구랑 킥킥거리며 웃다가 혼났어.
exampleEn: I got in trouble for giggling with my friend secretly behind the teacher's back.

meaningEn: (manner) grinning, smirking (often smug or up to something); pairs with 히죽거리다.
exampleKo: 재미있는 상상을 했는지 혼자 히죽히죽 웃고 있더라.
exampleEn: He must have imagined something funny because he was grinning to himself.

meaningEn: (manner) all smiles, beaming with visible happiness.
exampleKo: 좋은 소식이 있는지 아침부터 싱글벙글 웃고 있어.
exampleEn: She must have good news; she's been beaming with happiness since this morning.

meaningEn: (manner) smiling brightly and innocently; the word for a baby's smile; pairs with 방긋거리다.
exampleKo: 아기가 엄마를 보며 방긋방긋 예쁘게 웃었어.
exampleEn: The baby smiled brightly and innocently at its mom.

meaningEn: (sound) bawling out loud, crying without holding back; pairs with 울다.
exampleKo: 아기가 배고픈지 엉엉 울기 시작했어요.
exampleEn: The baby started to bawl, probably because it was hungry.

meaningEn: (sound) sniffling, quiet sobbing; also sniffing a runny nose. verb 훌쩍거리다. NOTE: single 훌쩍 = in one leap / all at once.
exampleKo: 영화가 슬펐는지 옆자리 친구가 훌쩍훌쩍 울고 있었어.
exampleEn: The movie must have been sad; my friend next to me was quietly sniffling.

meaningEn: (sound) whispering softly, heads close together. verb 소곤거리다.
exampleKo: 아이들이 서로 얼굴을 맞대고 소곤소곤 이야기했어요.
exampleEn: The children put their heads together and whispered softly.

meaningEn: (sound) whispering secretively, gossiping just out of earshot. verb 속닥거리다.
exampleKo: 저 사람들이 뭐 때문에 저렇게 속닥속닥 얘기할까?
exampleEn: What are those people secretly whispering about?

meaningEn: (sound) muttering to oneself under one's breath. verb 중얼거리다.
exampleKo: 혼자서 뭘 그렇게 중얼중얼해? 무슨 일 있어?
exampleEn: What are you muttering about to yourself? Is something wrong?

meaningEn: (sound) chattering away brightly; children or small birds. verb 재잘거리다.
exampleKo: 아이들이 학교 끝나고 재잘재잘 떠드는 소리가 들려요.
exampleEn: I can hear the children chattering brightly after school.

meaningEn: (sound) a crowd murmuring and buzzing, many voices at once. verb 웅성거리다.
exampleKo: 무슨 일인지 사람들이 모여서 웅성웅성하고 있었어.
exampleEn: People gathered, murmuring and buzzing, wondering what was happening.

meaningEn: (manner) clearly and distinctly, one syllable at a time; speaking, writing, or paying installments on time.
exampleKo: 아나운서는 말을 또박또박하게 잘하는 것 같아요.
exampleEn: Announcers seem to speak very clearly and distinctly.

meaningEn: (sound) crisp, fresh bite: apple, lettuce, fresh kimchi. verb 아삭거리다, adj 아삭하다.
exampleKo: 신선한 사과를 아삭아삭 소리 내면서 맛있게 먹었어요.
exampleEn: I ate the fresh apple, making a crisp crunching sound.

meaningEn: (sound) crunchy and dry-crisp: fried chicken, crackers, 전. adj 바삭하다.
exampleKo: 이 치킨은 튀김옷이 바삭바삭해서 정말 맛있어요.
exampleEn: This fried chicken is so delicious because the batter is perfectly crunchy.

meaningEn: (manner) chewy and springy in a good way: 떡, noodles, squid. adj 쫄깃하다. prized texture in Korean food.
exampleKo: 이 떡볶이 떡은 쫄깃쫄깃해서 식감이 너무 좋아요.
exampleEn: The rice cakes in this tteokbokki are so deliciously chewy.

meaningEn: (manner) pleasantly moist: cake, skin, damp grass. normally used as adj 촉촉하다; skincare-ad staple.
exampleKo: 이 크림을 바르니 피부가 촉촉하고 부드러워졌어요.
exampleEn: My skin became moist and soft after I applied this cream.

meaningEn: (sound) slurping noodles or soup in one go; not rude in Korea.
exampleKo: 배고파서 라면을 후루룩 소리 내면서 다 먹었어요.
exampleEn: I was so hungry that I slurped down all the ramen.

meaningEn: (sound) gulping down in one swallow; also swallowing hard from nerves.
exampleKo: 목이 말라서 물 한 잔을 꿀꺽 삼켰어요.
exampleEn: I was so thirsty I gulped down a whole glass of water.

meaningEn: (sound) yum-yum, munching happily; childlike and cute.
exampleKo: 아기가 밥을 냠냠 맛있게 먹는 모습이 귀여워요.
exampleEn: It's cute how the baby happily munches on its food.

meaningEn: (sound) crunching small hard bits: nuts, ice, 단무지. verb 오독거리다.
exampleKo: 땅콩을 오독오독 씹어 먹으니 고소하고 맛있어요.
exampleEn: Chewing the peanuts with a crunch is savory and delicious.

meaningEn: (sound) bubbling and simmering; the sound of 찌개 on the stove. verb 보글거리다.
exampleKo: 찌개가 냄비에서 보글보글 끓고 있어서 침이 고여요.
exampleEn: The jjigae is bubbling away in the pot, making my mouth water.

meaningEn: (sound) sizzling on a hot grill or pan; 삼겹살 cooking.
exampleKo: 불판 위에서 삼겹살이 지글지글 맛있게 익고 있어요.
exampleEn: The samgyeopsal is sizzling deliciously on the grill.

meaningEn: (sound) rain pouring down steadily in streams; also tears running down.
exampleKo: 어제 비가 하루 종일 주룩주룩 내렸어요.
exampleEn: It rained steadily all day yesterday.

meaningEn: (manner) drizzling softly, fine misty rain. 보슬비 = drizzle.
exampleKo: 날씨가 흐리고 보슬보슬 비가 내리고 있어요.
exampleEn: The weather is cloudy, and it's drizzling softly.

meaningEn: (sound) splashing about in water.
exampleKo: 아이들이 물웅덩이에서 첨벙첨벙 신나게 놀고 있었어요.
exampleEn: The children were happily splashing about in the puddles.

meaningEn: (sound) a small stream trickling; also trailing after someone closely (강아지처럼 졸졸 따라다니다).
exampleKo: 작은 시냇물이 졸졸 흐르는 소리가 들렸어요.
exampleEn: I heard the sound of a small stream trickling.

meaningEn: (manner) a breeze blowing gently; also a tail wagging. verb 살랑거리다.
exampleKo: 봄바람이 살랑살랑 불어와서 기분이 좋았어요.
exampleEn: The spring breeze blew gently, making me feel good.

meaningEn: (manner) flying freely on wide wings; also flames blazing up, or letting something go free.
exampleKo: 새들이 하늘 위로 훨훨 날아가는 모습이 아름다웠어요.
exampleEn: The sight of birds flying freely high in the sky was beautiful.

meaningEn: (manner) snow falling thickly; crying one's eyes out; spending money freely. (three common uses)
exampleKo: 밤새 눈이 펑펑 내려서 온 세상이 하얗게 변했어요.
exampleEn: Snow fell thickly all night, turning the whole world white.

meaningEn: (manner) air turning hot and stuffy; a face flushing with heat; pairs with 하다.
exampleKo: 방 안이 후끈후끈해서 창문을 좀 열어야겠어요.
exampleEn: The room is getting all hot and stuffy, so I should open the window.

meaningEn: (manner) toddling; a baby's first unsteady steps; pairs with 걷다.
exampleKo: 우리 아기가 아장아장 걷는 모습이 너무 귀여워요.
exampleEn: Our baby toddling around is so cute.

meaningEn: (manner) striding with long confident steps; a season arriving fast; pairs with 걷다 or 다가오다.
exampleKo: 그는 성큼성큼 걸어서 금방 우리에게 다가왔어.
exampleEn: He strode quickly and came over to us in no time.

meaningEn: (manner) ambling around with no purpose, or a predator prowling; pairs with 걷다 or 거리다.
exampleKo: 길고양이가 골목을 어슬렁어슬렁 돌아다니고 있었어요.
exampleEn: A stray cat was ambling aimlessly around the alley.

meaningEn: (manner) sneaking quietly so no one notices; pairs with 걷다 or 움직이다.
exampleKo: 엄마 몰래 냉장고로 살금살금 가서 아이스크림을 꺼냈어.
exampleEn: I snuck quietly to the fridge without Mom knowing and took out some ice cream.

meaningEn: (manner) dashing off or finishing something in a quick burst; pairs with 가다 or 해치우다.
exampleKo: 비가 오기 전에 빨래를 후다닥 걷어 왔어요.
exampleEn: I quickly dashed out and brought in the laundry before it rained.

meaningEn: (manner) staggering, unsteady on one's feet; pairs with 걷다 or 거리다.
exampleKo: 술에 취해서 비틀비틀 걷는 사람이 보였어요.
exampleEn: I saw someone staggering unsteadily, drunk from alcohol.

meaningEn: (manner) trudging wearily, heavy dragging steps after a hard day; pairs with 걷다.
exampleKo: 힘든 하루를 보내고 터벅터벅 집으로 돌아왔어요.
exampleEn: After a tough day, I trudged wearily back home.

meaningEn: (manner) hopping; a rabbit's movement; pairs with 뛰다.
exampleKo: 토끼가 풀밭에서 깡충깡충 뛰어다니는 모습이 귀엽네요.
exampleEn: The rabbit hopping around in the grass looks cute.

meaningEn: (manner) waddling side to side; a penguin or duck; pairs with 걷다 or 거리다.
exampleKo: 아기 오리들이 엄마를 따라 뒤뚱뒤뚱 걸어가요.
exampleEn: Baby ducklings waddle along, following their mom.

meaningEn: (manner) spinning round and round smoothly; a head spinning; pairs with 돌다 or 돌리다.
exampleKo: 컵이 빙글빙글 돌다가 바닥으로 떨어졌어요.
exampleEn: The cup spun round and round before falling to the floor.

meaningEn: (sound) sleeping deeply, snoring; the Korean 'zzz'; pairs with 자다.
exampleKo: 아기가 침대에서 쿨쿨 자고 있어서 방해하지 마.
exampleEn: The baby is sleeping soundly in bed, so don't disturb him.

meaningEn: (manner) nodding off, head bobbing with sleep; pairs with 졸다. NOTE: single 꾸벅 is a quick bow.
exampleKo: 수업 시간에 꾸벅꾸벅 졸아서 선생님께 혼났어요.
exampleEn: I nodded off repeatedly during class and got scolded by the teacher.

meaningEn: (manner) rolling around doing absolutely nothing; lazy-weekend word; pairs with 하다 or 거리다.
exampleKo: 주말에는 집에서 뒹굴뒹굴 영화 보는 게 최고야.
exampleEn: On weekends, just rolling around at home watching movies is the best.

meaningEn: (manner) blankly, staring into space; pairs with 있다 or 쳐다보다. 멍때리다 = to zone out.
exampleKo: 피곤해서 멍하니 창밖만 바라보고 있었어요.
exampleEn: I was so tired, I just stared blankly out the window.

meaningEn: (manner) fidgeting or wriggling slowly; small restless movements of fingers/toes; pairs with 움직이다 or 거리다.
exampleKo: 아기가 발가락을 꼼지락꼼지락 움직이는 게 너무 귀여워.
exampleEn: The baby wiggling its toes is so cute.

meaningEn: (manner) a deep throbbing ache; sore muscles, a bruise; pairs with 아프다 or 거리다.
exampleKo: 어제 운동했더니 다리가 욱신욱신 아파요.
exampleEn: My legs are throbbing from exercising yesterday.

meaningEn: (manner) a splitting headache pounding; pairs with 아프다 or 하다.
exampleKo: 스트레스 때문에 머리가 지끈지끈 아파서 약을 먹었어요.
exampleEn: My head was pounding from stress, so I took some medicine.

meaningEn: (manner) sharp little stabs of pain; also poking someone repeatedly; pairs with 쑤시다 or 찌르다.
exampleKo: 옆구리가 콕콕 쑤셔서 병원에 가봐야겠어요.
exampleEn: My side is having sharp little pains, so I should go to the hospital.

meaningEn: (manner) stinging, prickling; a sore throat, sunburn, injection; pairs with 아프다 or 거리다.
exampleKo: 햇볕에 타서 피부가 따끔따끔해요.
exampleEn: My skin is stinging from the sunburn.

meaningEn: (manner) ticklish, a light itch on the skin; pairs with 하다 or 거리다. 간지럽히다 = to tickle.
exampleKo: 목 뒤가 간질간질해서 자꾸 긁게 돼요.
exampleEn: The back of my neck feels ticklish, so I keep scratching it.

meaningEn: (manner) dizzy, the room spinning; pairs with 하다.
exampleKo: 너무 오래 서 있었더니 머리가 어질어질해요.
exampleEn: I stood for too long, and now my head feels dizzy.

meaningEn: (manner) queasy, stomach churning with nausea or nerves; pairs with 하다 or 거리다.
exampleKo: 멀미 때문에 속이 울렁울렁해서 아무것도 못 먹겠어요.
exampleEn: I'm so nauseous from motion sickness that I can't eat anything.

meaningEn: (sound) a bang or slam; a door slamming, a crash; pairs with 닫다 or 부딪히다. Often doubled as 쾅쾅.
exampleKo: 바람 때문에 문이 쾅 하고 닫혔어요.
exampleEn: The wind made the door slam shut with a bang.

meaningEn: (sound) a heavy thud; something big hitting the floor; pairs with 떨어지다 or 부딪히다. 쿵쾅쿵쾅 = stomping.
exampleKo: 위층에서 뭔가 쿵 하고 떨어지는 소리가 났어.
exampleEn: There was a heavy thud from upstairs, like something fell.

meaningEn: (sound) knocking on a door or dripping in drops; pairs with 두드리다 (knock) or 떨어지다 (drip). NOTE: homonym 똑똑하다 means 'to be smart'.
exampleKo: 문에서 똑똑 소리가 나서 누구인지 궁금했어요.
exampleEn: I heard a knock-knock sound at the door and wondered who it was.

meaningEn: (sound) creaking of an old door or floorboard; also used for a relationship/plan hitting friction. Pairs with 거리다 or 나다.
exampleKo: 오래된 마루에서 걸을 때마다 삐걱삐걱 소리가 나요.
exampleEn: Every time I walk on the old wooden floor, it makes a creaking sound.

meaningEn: (sound) rustling of paper, dry leaves, or a plastic snack bag; pairs with 거리다 or 소리 나다.
exampleKo: 밤에 누가 과자 봉지를 부스럭부스럭 뜯는 소리가 났어요.
exampleEn: At night, I heard someone rustling a snack bag.

meaningEn: (sound) the crash of something shattering all at once (dishes, glass); pairs with 깨지다 or 떨어지다.
exampleKo: 접시가 바닥에 떨어져 와장창 깨지는 소리가 들렸어요.
exampleEn: I heard the plates fall to the floor and shatter with a crash.

meaningEn: (sound) coins or keys jingling in a pocket; pairs with 거리다 or 소리 나다.
exampleKo: 주머니에서 동전이 짤랑짤랑 소리를 내며 흔들렸어요.
exampleEn: The coins in my pocket jingled and rattled.

meaningEn: (sound) a small bell ringing (e.g., shop door chime, cat's collar); pairs with 울리다 or 소리 나다.
exampleKo: 고양이 목에 달린 방울이 딸랑딸랑 소리를 냈어요.
exampleEn: The bell on the cat's neck made a ding-a-ling sound.

meaningEn: (sound) dripping in fat drops (tears, water); also something snapping off. Pairs with 떨어지다 or 흐르다. Used with 그치다 (stop abruptly).
exampleKo: 수도꼭지에서 물방울이 뚝뚝 떨어지는 소리가 밤새 들렸어요.
exampleEn: I heard water drops dripping all night from the faucet.

meaningEn: (sound) a dog barking: woof woof; pairs with 짖다 (bark). Often used as 멍멍이 for 'doggy'.
exampleKo: 옆집 개가 밤새 멍멍 짖어서 잠을 잘 수 없었어요.
exampleEn: The dog next door barked "woof woof" all night, so I couldn't sleep.

meaningEn: (sound) a cat meowing: meow; pairs with 울다 (cry/meow). Often used as 야옹이 for 'kitty'.
exampleKo: 배고픈 아기 고양이가 야옹 소리를 내며 엄마를 찾았어요.
exampleEn: The hungry kitten meowed, looking for its mom.

meaningEn: (sound) a small bird chirping: tweet tweet, chirp chirp; pairs with 울다 (cry/chirp).
exampleKo: 아침에 창문 밖에서 새들이 짹짹 노래하는 소리가 들렸어요.
exampleEn: In the morning, I heard birds chirping outside the window.

meaningEn: (sound) a pig: oink oink; pairs with 울다 (cry/oink). Often used as 꿀꿀이 for 'piggy'.
exampleKo: 돼지가 밥 달라고 꿀꿀 소리를 내며 우리를 쳐다봤어요.
exampleEn: The pig oinked and looked at us, asking for food.

meaningEn: (sound) a cow: moo; pairs with 울다 (cry/moo).
exampleKo: 넓은 초원에서 소들이 음매 울며 풀을 뜯고 있었어요.
exampleEn: In the wide pasture, cows were mooing and grazing.

meaningEn: (sound) a frog: ribbit ribbit; pairs with 울다 (cry/ribbit).
exampleKo: 연못가에서 개구리들이 개굴개굴 소리를 내며 합창했어요.
exampleEn: By the pond, the frogs were ribbiting in chorus.

meaningEn: (sound) a baby chick: peep peep; pairs with 울다 (cry/peep).
exampleKo: 병아리들이 엄마를 따라다니며 삐약삐약 울었어요.
exampleEn: The chicks followed their mom, peeping.

meaningEn: (sound) a rooster: cock-a-doodle-doo; pairs with 울다 (cry/crow).
exampleKo: 새벽마다 수탉이 꼬끼오 하고 울어서 잠을 깼어요.
exampleEn: Every dawn, the rooster crowed "cock-a-doodle-doo" and woke me up.

meaningEn: (manner) round and roundish, lots of small round things; pairs with 하다 (동글동글하다) or 생기다 (look round).
exampleKo: 아기 얼굴이 너무 동글동글해서 귀여워요.
exampleEn: The baby's face is so round and cute.

meaningEn: (manner) bumpy and uneven (a rough road, muscles); pairs with 하다 (울퉁불퉁하다) or 생기다 (look bumpy).
exampleKo: 산길은 울퉁불퉁해서 조심해서 걸어야 해요.
exampleEn: The mountain path is bumpy and uneven, so you have to walk carefully.

meaningEn: (manner) slippery, slick to the touch (a wet floor, soap); pairs with 하다 (미끌미끌하다) or 거리다.
exampleKo: 비가 와서 바닥이 미끌미끌하니까 조심하세요.
exampleEn: The floor is slippery because of the rain, so be careful.

meaningEn: (manner) limp and mushy, falling apart (overcooked noodles); pairs with 하다 (흐물흐물하다) or 해지다 (become mushy).
exampleKo: 라면을 너무 오래 끓였더니 흐물흐물해져서 맛이 없어요.
exampleEn: I boiled the ramen for too long, and now it's mushy and doesn't taste good.

meaningEn: (manner) soft and smooth to the touch (a baby's cheek, fine fabric); pairs with 하다 (보들보들하다).
exampleKo: 아기 피부가 보들보들해서 계속 만지고 싶어요.
exampleEn: The baby's skin is so soft and smooth, I want to keep touching it.

meaningEn: (manner) fluffy and cushiony (a thick sofa, a duvet); pairs with 하다 (푹신푹신하다).
exampleKo: 이 소파는 너무 푹신푹신해서 앉으면 잠이 와요.
exampleEn: This sofa is so fluffy and cushiony that I feel sleepy when I sit on it.

meaningEn: (manner) sticky and tacky (honey, sweaty summer air); pairs with 하다 (끈적끈적하다) or 거리다.
exampleKo: 더운 여름날에는 피부가 끈적끈적해서 불쾌해요.
exampleEn: On hot summer days, my skin feels sticky and uncomfortable.

meaningEn: (manner) pointy and spiky all over (a cactus, mountain peaks); pairs with 하다 (뾰족뾰족하다) or 생기다. Note: adj is 뾰족하다.
exampleKo: 선인장에는 뾰족뾰족한 가시가 많으니 조심하세요.
exampleEn: Cacti have lots of pointy spines, so be careful.

meaningEn: (manner) covered in tiny bumps (goosebumps, a bumpy rind); pairs with 하다 (오돌토돌하다) or 돋다 (for goosebumps).
exampleKo: 추워서 팔에 오돌토돌 소름이 돋았어요.
exampleEn: I was so cold that I got goosebumps all over my arms.

meaningEn: (manner) glossy, polished smooth and shiny (a waxed floor, slicked hair); pairs with 하다 (반들반들하다) or 거리다.
exampleKo: 깨끗하게 닦은 바닥이 반들반들 윤이 났어요.
exampleEn: The freshly cleaned floor was glossy and shiny.
